COREFORGE THIRD-PARTY NOTICES
=============================

This generated, self-contained aggregate accompanies Coreforge release artifacts.
It does not replace package-level license files. First-party licensing grants
no rights in third-party code, fonts, data, or marks identified below.

PYTHON DEPENDENCY DISTRIBUTION ROLE
===================================

omp-rpc has no third-party runtime dependencies. robomp declares FastAPI,
Uvicorn, HTTPX, Pydantic, pydantic-settings, python-dotenv, Click, and omp-rpc
as ordinary installer-resolved dependencies. The Python wheels do not vendor
those projects; each dependency remains a separately installed distribution
carrying its own license metadata and files. Container/system assemblers must
retain those independently installed distributions' notices.

TRACKED VENDORED CODE AND ASSET NOTICES
=======================================

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
crates/pi-builtins/LICENSE

This crate hosts the in-process command-line utility builtins (`src/host.rs`
plus one module per command). Those are ports of third-party programs, previously
carried as separate vendored crates and now consolidated here; the host plumbing
is ours, the utility logic is theirs. Their notices are reproduced in full
below.

crates/pi-shell/NOTICE

This file documents third-party attribution for the shell-output minimizer in
this crate, which adapts an algorithm from RTK (https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk),
used under the MIT License.

  Copyright (c) the RTK authors (rtk-ai/rtk)

Adapted component: the `build_pytest_summary` algorithm from the upstream
`src/cmds/python/pytest_cmd.rs` (pinned at commit
878af7de99e0ba71da2e8fd996f6b52a1836e06c), re-implemented here in
`src/minimizer/filters/python.rs` as the pytest state machine (`filter_pytest`,
`pytest_success`, `is_pytest_*`, `looks_like_pytest_summary_part`). It preserves
failures, errors, and the final summary line; strips header framing, progress
dots, and verbose `PASSED` rows; and falls through unchanged on unknown-state
lines (RTK's defensive default) so xdist `[gwN]` prefixes and custom reporters
never cause data loss.

MIT License

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:

copies or substantial portions of the Software.

packages/utils/src/vendor/mermaid-ascii/NOTICE

This directory contains an in-house Mermaid-diagram-to-ASCII renderer adapted
from beautiful-mermaid (https://github.com/lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid), used
under the MIT License.

  Copyright (c) 2026 Craft Docs

Only the ASCII rendering pipeline is ported (flowchart/state, sequence, class,
ER, and xychart diagrams); the SVG renderer and its `elkjs` graph-layout
dependency, the browser entry point, and the SVG theme/style modules were
dropped. Terminal display width is reimplemented on `Bun.stringWidth`, and
inline label formatting (HTML tags, markdown emphasis) is reduced to plain text
for ASCII output. Layout and edge-routing logic is preserved faithfully so
ASCII output matches the upstream package.

of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell

crates/vendor/cranelift-codegen/COREFORGE-PATCHES.md

# Maintained Cranelift security backport

This directory contains the exact `cranelift-codegen` 0.116.1 registry source, plus the changes listed below.

- Archive: <https://static.crates.io/crates/cranelift-codegen/cranelift-codegen-0.116.1.crate>
- Archive SHA-256: `2c22032c4cb42558371cf516bb47f26cdad1819d3475c133e93c49f50ebf304e`
- Archive size: 1,051,844 bytes.
- Original VCS commit: `58282df898d79a787a726d829b166272dde155b9`.
- Original VCS path: `cranelift/codegen`.
- License: `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`. Preserve the complete original `LICENSE` and source notices.

The original `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, manifests, lockfile, README and license remain unchanged. The archive contains 201 members. `BUILD.bazel`, `rustfmt.toml`, this provenance file and `patches/0001-full-value-indices.patch` are local additions.

`rustfmt.toml` uses the existing vendored-crate policy to preserve upstream source formatting. It does not exclude unit, integration or feature tests.

## Maintained source change

`patches/0001-full-value-indices.patch` records every change to `src/ir/dfg.rs` against the original archive. It backports the private `ValueDataPacked` representation from maintainer commit [ba8f7d70caa1825b7f64fa75cd9d03f4a438dae0](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/commit/ba8f7d70caa1825b7f64fa75cd9d03f4a438dae0). The representation retains full `u32` entity indices instead of narrowing them to 24 bits. Its tag and type fields remain 16 bits together.

This addresses the Cranelift bit-packing defect described in [GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/security/advisories/GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm). It does not upgrade Wasmtime 29.0.1 or resolve all advisories against that runtime.

The same patch adds small direct representation tests around the former 24-bit boundary and the reserved sentinel. It also tests type changes without losing definition indices. The serialization roundtrip uses the existing optional `postcard` dependency under `incremental-cache`, which enables `enable-serde`. These tests do not compile malicious or oversized WebAssembly.

## Build ownership

The root Cargo workspace and patch declaration select this source for Cargo and Bazel. `BUILD.bazel` preserves the production feature set: `gimli`, `host-arch`, `std`, `timing`, and `unwind`.

The original `build.rs` must run for each target. It consumes `TARGET`, generates Rust and ISLE output into `OUT_DIR`, and supplies the ISA configuration and `ISLE_DIR`. Its build dependencies are `cranelift-codegen-meta` 0.116.1 and `cranelift-isle` 0.116.1. No generated host output replaces those inputs.

The Bazel build script sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` and `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`. It sets `GIT_DIR=.` to the non-repository crate directory. The original script then uses its package-version fallback without discovering host checkout metadata. No `.git` input is required.

Regenerate workspace locks and aliases from the root declarations. Preserve the license in distribution notices. Qualify the source through the repository's canonical Cargo, Bazel, native-addon and supported-target checks. Include debug and release boundary tests, `enable-serde` compilation, and `incremental-cache` serialization tests.

## Updating

1. Verify a replacement registry archive against its recorded checksum.
2. Preserve its original provenance and complete license.
3. Apply the maintained patch to that exact source, or remove it only when upstream provides the full index guarantee.
4. Update portable build dependencies and target features from the resolved graph.
5. Regenerate locks and aliases through the canonical root tools.
6. Qualify the actual linked source and the affected supported targets before claiming the correction is complete.

ROOT LOCK AND SEPARATE ON-DEMAND INSTALLATIONS
---------------------------------------------
The root lock selects fastembed 3.0.0, onnxruntime-node 1.21.0,
@anush008/tokenizers 0.0.0, and its three 0.0.0 platform packages:
@anush008/tokenizers-darwin-universal, @anush008/tokenizers-linux-x64-gnu,
and @anush008/tokenizers-win32-x64-msvc. These runtime-external identities
and their root-lock dependencies are listed separately from bundled code.
They do not describe the separately resolved on-demand installation graph.

The fastembed on-demand installer requests fastembed 3.0.0 and overrides
@anush008/tokenizers to 0.6.0. The speech/tiny installer separately requests
@huggingface/transformers 4.3.0. The Kokoro installer requests kokoro-js 1.2.1
and overrides onnxruntime-node to 1.26.0. These are user-side package-manager
installations. Coreforge bundles do not redistribute those downloaded
implementations. Their resolved transitive trees are not this root inventory.
Original package notices must remain with separately installed dependencies.

The current root lock contains no sharp or @img/sharp-libvips-* identities.
The old sharp-libvips 1.3.3 family is not current root-lock membership.
If a separate optional installation selects LGPL-covered libvips, retain its
license and corresponding-source availability. The dynamically loaded native
library remains replaceable. Upstream sources are available from
https://github.com/lovell/sharp-libvips.git and the upstream libvips project.

Exact public npm metadata declares MIT for the four tokenizer 0.0.0 packages.
Their declared source revision is 6257e92b2d77bec979e92533b8aa0ba2466d3c76
at https://github.com/Anush008/tokenizers. That revision has no standalone

A. HISTORY OF THE SOFTWARE
==========================

Python was created in the early 1990s by Guido van Rossum at Stichting
Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands
as a successor of a language called ABC.  Guido remains Python's
principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

In 1995, Guido continued his work on Python at the Corporation for
National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
Zope Corporation was a sponsoring member of the PSF.

All Python releases are Open Source (see http://www.opensource.org for
the Open Source Definition).  Historically, most, but not all, Python
releases have also been GPL-compatible; the table below summarizes
the various releases.

    Release         Derived     Year        Owner       GPL-
                    from                                compatible? (1)

    0.9.0 thru 1.2              1991-1995   CWI         yes
    1.3 thru 1.5.2  1.2         1995-1999   CNRI        yes
    1.6             1.5.2       2000        CNRI        no
    2.0             1.6         2000        BeOpen.com  no
    1.6.1           1.6         2001        CNRI        yes (2)
    2.1             2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         no
    2.0.1           2.0+1.6.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.1           2.1+2.0.1   2001        PSF         yes
    2.1.2           2.1.1       2002        PSF         yes
    2.1.3           2.1.2       2002        PSF         yes
    2.2 and above   2.1.1       2001-now    PSF         yes

Footnotes:

(1) GPL-compatible doesn't mean that we're distributing Python under
    the GPL.  All Python licenses, unlike the GPL, let you distribute
    a modified version without making your changes open source.  The
    GPL-compatible licenses make it possible to combine Python with
    other software that is released under the GPL; the others don't.

(2) According to Richard Stallman, 1.6.1 is not GPL-compatible,
    because its license has a choice of law clause.  According to
    CNRI, however, Stallman's lawyer has told CNRI's lawyer that 1.6.1
    is "not incompatible" with the GPL.

Thanks to the many outside volunteers who have worked under Guido's
direction to make these releases possible.
